neighbours.label: Sentences written in a language other than English: strongest in Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Greek, Thai and Vietnamese (about 0.4-0.8 of max), weaker in German, Spanish and French (about 0.2-0.3); quiet on everyday English prose, though a rare English word the tokenizer splits into odd pieces can reach about 0.3, and a single foreign word dropped into an English sentence is unreliable
neighbours.notes: Gate-closed echo pole (-g +u leak 100%), dense (18.9% of tokens >0.1 max). Corpus tops are word-internal pieces in CJK/Korean/Cyrillic text (rare byte-split characters like 勵 reach ~0.84). Reader of L31/N8934+ (German einz-) with a near-zero ablation drop; German 'einzige' sits at ~0.25, peak on ' einz'. Feeders (L0/N4077+, L28/N9308+) are CJK character cells. Test sentences written blind by a label-only author.
